NSC 510.name: Systems Neuroscience
NSC 510.description: Neural regulation of sensory and motor systems. Functions such as vision, audition, olfaction, gustation, motor movement, reproduction, sleep and biological rhythms, emotion, learning and memory and psychopathology.

NSC 511.name: Cellular, Molecular and Developmental Neuroscience
NSC 511.description: The fundamental principles underlying neuronal biophysics; molecular, cellular and developmental processes. Cellular components of nervous tissue, membrane and action potentials, neurotransmitter regulation and intracellular signaling, neural induction and pattern formation, neurogenesis, migration and synaptic regulation.

NSC 512.name: Research Methods in Neuroscience
NSC 512.description: Behavioral experimental design and analysis. Computational Modeling. Neural Networks. Molecular and cellular methods in neurons.

NSC 513.name: Behavioral Neuroscience
NSC 513.description: Seminar course in which students read a wide range of articles that relate to the overview of the neurological processes underlying organismic behavior. Survey on neurobiological explanations of topics such as sensation, movement, motivation, emotion, sleep, learning, neurological disorders, and recovery mechanisms.

NSC 514.name: Affective Neuroscience
NSC 514.description: Biological basis of emotion. Overview of and historical basis for the field of affective neuroscience. Mapping affective experience and behavior to brain function, including cross-level integration of anatomical, chemical, and electrical data.

NSC 515.name: Computational and Numerical Methods in Neuroscience
NSC 515.description: Basic mathematical techniques for analysis and modeling of neural systems. Various methods in this highly active field are discussed.

NSC 516.name: Neurobiology of Aging
NSC 516.description: Biological basis of aging and neurodegenerative disease. Current cellular and brain imaging tools as they relate to understanding the aging and neurodegenerative disease process. Recent advances in research techniques related to aging and neurodegenerative disease.

NSC 517.name: Neuroanatomy
NSC 517.description: The study of the nervous system, its structure, and function is known as neuroanatomy. This course examines the anatomy of the central and peripheral nervous systems in detail, including the brain, spinal cord, cranial nerves, and vascular structures. Students will discover how neurons are organized and connected, as well as the importance of supporting structures. The course will begin with an overview of basic neuroanatomical terminology, then the primary anatomical structures and processes involved in sensory perception, motor control, autonomic organization, and higher cognitive functions for instance, learning, memory, emotion, and language will be covered in this course. Students will also develop an understanding of the relationship between neuroanatomy and brain function, which will enable them to critically evaluate research findings in the field of neuroscience. The course will be provided in the form of lectures, interactive activities, and video demonstrations. Some lectures can be supported with anatomical models, if necessary, due to understanding of the 3D structure. Students will have a good foundation in the anatomy and function of the nervous system after completing this course, which will be valuable for further study in subjects such as neuroscience, psychology, and medicine.

NSC 518.name: Basic Mechanism of Nervous System Disorders
NSC 518.description: An overview of the fundamental mechanisms underlying both organic and mental disorders of the nervous system. It covers cellular mechanisms involved in acute and chronic injury, as well as the processes of protein aggregation and dysfunction within neuronal networks.

NSC 519.name: Comparative Cognitive Neuroscience
NSC 519.description: Neuronal basis of cognition across a wide range of species; emergence of spatial navigation, perception, learning, memory, attention, and decision-making from neural circuits; structural and functional requirements for complex cognitive functions; insights into the evolutionary origins and diversity of cognition through studies of "simple" organisms.

NSC 539.name: Visual Neuroscience
NSC 539.description: Visual science, a model and reference for all other areas in neuroscience, has seen remarkable advances in the last decade. This course covers selected topics in the study of the visual system in great detail through review of recent literature. Topics covered vary and include retinal mechanisms, visual pathways, subcortical and cortical processing, lightness and color, motion perception, object recognition, eye movements and attention. The course also emphasizes methods used to study the biological visual system.

NSC 546.name: Computing for Neuroscience
NSC 546.description: Experimental design and control in systems neuroscience, basics of signal processing, generating images, movies and sounds, basics of optimization and curve fitting, functions for statistical testing and bootstrapping, use of Matlab programming for neural signal processing, signal detection theory, receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis.

NSC 591.name: Pro-thesis Seminar I
NSC 591.description: Presentations on the current and classical literature.

NSC 599.name: Neuroscience Master's Thesis
NSC 599.description: A research-based thesis course in which the student will complete a comprehensive, individual hypothesis-driven project. The topic will be agreed upon in consultation with the supervisor. The project will be of suitable complexity for the results to be defended in both oral and written format in front of an expert audience.

NSC 612.name: Selected Topics in Neuroscience I
NSC 612.description: Current topics in neuroscience. Survey of the literature related to a current selected topic of interest.

NSC 613.name: Selected Topics in Neuroscience II
NSC 613.description: Current topics in neuroscience. Survey of the literature related to a current selected topic of interest.

NSC 670.name: Lab in Cellular, Molecular, and Developmental Neuroscience
NSC 670.description: Experimental approaches in cellular, molecular and developmental neuroscience. Experiments on cell structure and organization of the vertebrate central nervous system, and mechanisms underlying neural signaling and plasticity. Laboratory instruction in anatomical, physiological, and biochemical methods for investigating the biology of nerve cells.

NSC 671.name: Lab in Sensory and Motor Systems Neuroscience
NSC 671.description: Experimental approaches in sensory and motor systems neuroscience. Laboratory instruction in neuroanatomy, sensory neurophysiology, modern neuroanatomical tracer techniques, psychophysics, and computational neuroscience.

NSC 672.name: Applied Magnetic Resonance Imaging for Neuroscience
NSC 672.description: Hemodynamic response and its characteristics, experimental design principles, fMRI data simulation and analysis, fMRI data acquisition, preprocessing, first and second level univariate analyses, group analyses, multivariate analyses, connectivity analyses.

NSC 691.name: Pro-thesis Seminar II
NSC 691.description: Presentations on the current and classical literature.

NSC 699.name: Neuroscience Ph.D. Dissertation
NSC 699.description: A research-based dissertation course in which the student will complete a comprehensive, individual hypothesis-driven thesis project. The topic will be agreed upon in consultation with the supervisor and approved and followed by a supervising thesis committee. The project will be of suitable complexity for the results to be defended in both an oral and written format in front of an expert audience and should result in a publication in an ISI-indexed journal.
